title: Animal Classification Tree
subtitle: Put animals on the right branches
learningGoals: Know that animals can be grouped in different ways.
Understand vertebrates and invertebrates at a first level.
Use clues such as feathers, fur, gills, scales, and legs to classify animals.
misconceptions: Every animal that lives in water is a fish.

hero.title: Animal Classification Tree
hero.lead: The animal world is like a big tree. Each animal lives on its own branch.
hero.sceneExplanation: The main scene is a layered tree: the root is ‘animals’, the first split is vertebrates and invertebrates, and the branches continue into mammals, birds, fish, reptiles, amphibians, insects, and more. When a child clicks an animal card, the matching branch lights up.
hero.childPrompt: Tap an animal card and see which branch it belongs to.
hero.parentPrompt: The goal is not to memorize category names. Help the child explain the clue used for sorting: body structure, breathing, babies, or lifestyle.

classificationGroups.name: Vertebrates
classificationGroups.childExplanation: Animals with an important bone column inside the body, like a body support.
classificationGroups.parentNote: Use this as a child-friendly way to introduce the spine.
classificationGroups.misconception: Not every animal in water is a fish. A whale is a vertebrate, but it is a mammal.

classificationGroups.name: Mammals
classificationGroups.childExplanation: Many baby mammals drink milk from their mothers, and many have hair or fur.
classificationGroups.parentNote: Whales and bats are useful examples: classification is not only about where an animal lives or whether it flies.
classificationGroups.misconception: A whale is not a fish. A bat is not a bird.

classificationGroups.name: Birds
classificationGroups.childExplanation: Birds have feathers. Many birds can fly, but not all birds fly well.
classificationGroups.parentNote: Feathers are a better clue than flying.
classificationGroups.misconception: An animal that can fly is not always a bird, such as a bat.

classificationGroups.name: Fish
classificationGroups.childExplanation: Most fish live in water and breathe with gills.
classificationGroups.parentNote: For this age, use water + gills + fins as simple clues.
classificationGroups.misconception: Living in water does not always mean fish.

classificationGroups.name: Reptiles
classificationGroups.childExplanation: Reptiles often have scales. Many move close to the ground.
classificationGroups.parentNote: Avoid using ‘crawls’ as the only clue.
classificationGroups.misconception: Not every animal that crawls is a reptile.

classificationGroups.name: Amphibians
classificationGroups.childExplanation: Some amphibians live in water when young and can also live on land when grown.
classificationGroups.parentNote: Frogs are the easiest starting example.
classificationGroups.misconception: A frog is not a reptile.

classificationGroups.name: Insects
classificationGroups.childExplanation: Insects usually have six legs and three body parts.
classificationGroups.parentNote: This connects naturally to the insects-and-spiders topic.
classificationGroups.misconception: A spider is not an insect.

representativeObjects.name: Cat
representativeObjects.childExplanation: A cat is a mammal. Baby cats drink milk from their mother.
representativeObjects.visualHint: fur, four legs, kittens drinking milk
representativeObjects.commonMisread: Sorting only by living at home.

representativeObjects.name: Whale
representativeObjects.childExplanation: A whale lives in the sea, but it is not a fish. It is a mammal.
representativeObjects.visualHint: sea life, breathes air, baby drinks milk
representativeObjects.commonMisread: Thinking every sea animal is a fish.

representativeObjects.name: Bat
representativeObjects.childExplanation: A bat can fly, but it is not a bird. It is a mammal.
representativeObjects.commonMisread: Thinking every flying animal is a bird.

representativeObjects.name: Sparrow
representativeObjects.childExplanation: A sparrow has feathers, so it is a bird.

representativeObjects.name: Penguin
representativeObjects.childExplanation: A penguin does not fly well, but it has feathers, so it is still a bird.

representativeObjects.name: Goldfish
representativeObjects.childExplanation: A goldfish lives in water and breathes with gills.
representativeObjects.commonMisread: Thinking all water animals are fish.

representativeObjects.name: Shark
representativeObjects.childExplanation: A shark is a fish with a body made for swimming.
representativeObjects.commonMisread: Thinking big sea animals are all the same kind.

representativeObjects.name: Snake
representativeObjects.childExplanation: A snake has scales and is a reptile.
representativeObjects.commonMisread: Thinking all long animals are worms.

representativeObjects.name: Turtle
representativeObjects.childExplanation: A turtle is a reptile with a shell.

representativeObjects.name: Frog
representativeObjects.childExplanation: A frog is an amphibian. It changes a lot as it grows.

representativeObjects.name: Butterfly
representativeObjects.childExplanation: A butterfly is an insect with six legs.
representativeObjects.commonMisread: Thinking wings are the only clue.

representativeObjects.name: Ant
representativeObjects.childExplanation: An ant is an insect with six legs.

mechanism.title: What clues do we use for classification?

steps.childExplanation: Does it have feathers, scales, fur, or six legs?
steps.parentNote: Guide the child to observe stable features first.

steps.childExplanation: Does it live in water, on land, or both?
steps.parentNote: Lifestyle is a helpful clue, but not the only clue.

steps.childExplanation: How the baby grows can also help us classify.
steps.parentNote: Milk-feeding, eggs, and body changes can be expanded later.

steps.shortTitle: Do not use one clue only
steps.childExplanation: Flying does not always mean bird. Living in water does not always mean fish.
steps.parentNote: This is the core thinking skill of the page.

comparePairs.title: Whale vs Fish
comparePairs.childConclusion: Living in the sea does not always mean fish.

comparePairs.title: Bat vs Bird
comparePairs.childConclusion: Flying does not always mean bird.

comparePairs.title: Penguin vs Sparrow
comparePairs.childConclusion: Flying is not the only clue for birds.

clickTasks.title: Which branch should a whale live on?
clickTasks.prompt: A whale lives in the sea, but what kind of animal is it?

wrongHints.fish: Living in water is not enough. A whale breathes air and feeds milk to its baby.
wrongHints.birds: A whale does not have feathers.

clickTasks.successCopy: Right! A whale lives in the sea, but it is a mammal.

clickTasks.title: Is a bat a bird?
clickTasks.prompt: It can fly, but what clue matters more?

wrongHints.bird: Flying is not the only clue. Birds have feathers; bats do not.

clickTasks.successCopy: Yes! A bat can fly, but it is still a mammal.

clickTasks.title: Find: who has feathers?
clickTasks.successCopy: You found the feather clue. Sparrows and penguins are both birds.
clickTasks.wrongHint: Look for feathers, not only wings.

clickTasks.title: What should we check when sorting animals?
clickTasks.successCopy: You sorted like a scientist: look, think, then compare.
clickTasks.wrongHint: Start with what you can see on the body.

speakTemplates: I think ____ belongs to ____ because it has ____.
____ looks like ____, but it is actually ____ because ____.
Today I found out: do not only look at ____. Also look at ____.
parentTips: Do not ask the child to memorize all categories at once. Ask them to explain the clue.
Ask: Which clue did you use? Is there a counterexample?
This page connects naturally to Insects and Spiders and Dinosaur Classification.
acceptanceCriteria: The child can name at least three animal groups.
The child can explain at least one misconception, such as why a whale is not a fish.
